learning_outcomes.text: Explains the architecture of a robotic system, its functional components, and their role in the overall system.
Describes the classification of industrial robots and their main application areas.
Explains coordinate transformations, rotation and translation matrices, Denavit-Hartenberg parameters, and how these concepts are used in robot modeling.
Describes the principles of forward and inverse kinematics for both serial and parallel manipulator robots.
Explains the notions of robot statics and dynamics, including Newton-Euler and Lagrange formulations used in motion modeling.
Explains fundamental trajectory planning algorithms for industrial robots.
Applies mathematical methods and digital tools for modeling the forward and inverse kinematics of a robot manipulator.
Uses specialized software (such as Matlab) for simulating robot positions, velocities, and trajectories.
Interprets the Jacobian matrix, identifies possible singularities, and evaluates their consequences on motion.
Analyzes and evaluates the static and dynamic behavior of a robot based on theoretical models.
Uses experimental and simulation tools for controlling robot position and motion.
Works effectively in multidisciplinary teams, taking responsibility for theoretical and laboratory activities.
Documents and argues technical solutions for problems in robotics kinematics or dynamics.
Develops autonomy in using simulation software and interpreting the obtained results.
Respects ethical norms, laboratory working rules, and requirements regarding the accuracy and correctness of modeling and measurements.

syllabus_topics: Introduction (Generalities, Definitions, History, Economic and social aspects of automation, Classification of robots, Applications of robots, Architecture of a robotic system, Importance of studying robotics, Course objective)

Structure of the mechanical system of a manipulator robot (Generalities, Structure of the guiding mechanism, Structure of the positioning mechanism (trajectory generator), Structure of orientation mechanisms, End effector)

Coordinate transformations (Generalities, Rotation matrix, Translation matrix, Homogeneous transformation matrix, Rodrigues' formula, Euler parameters, Composition of rotations. Quaternions, Euler angles)
Forward kinematics of positions for manipulator robots (Introduction, Denavit-Hartenberg parameters, Homogeneous transformation matrix corresponding to an element)
Inverse kinematics of positions for manipulator robots

Velocity distribution. Jacobian matrix (Introduction, Velocity distribution in a rigid body, Virtual configuration modification, Relationship between angular velocity and rotation parameters, Velocity Jacobian, Inverse Jacobian matrix, singularity)
Statics of manipulator robots (Static forces and moments in manipulator robots, Calculation of forces and moments for a 3-DOF serial manipulator)
Dynamics of manipulator robots (Rigid body dynamics, Lagrange formulation, Newton-Euler formulation, Dynamic models of simple serial manipulator robot structures)
Architecture of a robot and structural analysis of the mechanical system
Direct kinematic analysis of the positions of a serial manipulator robot
Computer simulation of the direct kinematics of positions of a serial manipulator
Position control of a serial robot using direct kinematics results
Inverse kinematic analysis of the positions of a serial manipulator robot
Computer simulation of the inverse kinematics of positions of a serial manipulator robot
Position control of a serial robot using inverse kinematics results
Direct kinematic analysis of the velocities of a serial manipulator robot; Calculation of the Jacobian matrix
Direct and inverse kinematics of positions of a parallel manipulator robot; Computer simulation
Motion control of an RRR-type parallel robot
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with explanations and visual demonstrations, using multimedia presentations
Guided discussions, problem-solving, analysis of practical examples
Whiteboard demonstrations on coordinate transformations and kinematic models
Whiteboard presentation of the studied issues
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes and the granting of associated study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for the Examination/Verification components (formative and summative tests combined) and for the Laboratory activity.
